UI Preview Extension: Startup Performance Impact Analysis (Windows)

Extension under test: salesforcedx-vscode-ui-preview v1.1.4

Test project: dreamhouse (Dreamhouse LWC sample app)

Platform: Windows 11 (VM) -- VS Code 1.106.2, AMD EPYC 7763 (4 cores), 16 GB RAM

Context: Extension pack validation ahead of TDX. Windows counterpart to the macOS test. macOS used mega-enterprise; Windows uses dreamhouse, so absolute times are not directly comparable across platforms.

Without Run 1 Cold-Start Outlier: Without R1 shows significantly elevated Load Code for many extensions (e.g., vscode-agents 2,129 ms vs. 1,139-1,183 ms in R2/R3; vscode-lwc 2,199 ms vs. 585-616 ms). This is a classic first-run cold-cache effect on Windows VM. All "with" runs and Without R2/R3 show stable values. The 3-run averages in the tables below are skewed by this outlier; the conclusion uses R2/R3 comparison for accuracy.

Notes

  • apex-language-server-extension did not activate in Without R3 (no Apex file was opened to trigger onLanguage:apex). Its averages use R1/R2 only for the "without" scenario.
  • The dreamhouse project activates extensions not seen in the macOS mega-enterprise test: vscode-lightning, salesforce-vscode-slds, and salesforce-metadata-visualizer-vscode (which activated on XML files in dreamhouse).
  • salesforcedx-vscode-apex-testing shows elevated Call Activate on Windows (21-53 ms) compared to macOS (7-8 ms), likely due to VM overhead.

** Again driven by the Without R1 cold-start outlier. Key observations on individual extensions:

  • salesforcedx-vscode-apex (-5,874 ms / -28%): Extremely high variance on Windows (12,981-31,688 ms without; 14,280-16,209 ms with). The Without R1 value of 31,688 ms is a clear outlier. R2/R3 comparison: Without avg 15,586 ms vs. With avg 15,478 ms -- essentially flat.
  • salesforcedx-vscode-lightning (+1,299 ms / +65%): The With R1 value of 6,096 ms is an outlier (vs. 1,694/2,127 in R2/R3). R2/R3 comparison: Without avg 1,850 ms vs. With avg 1,911 ms (+3%) -- flat.
  • salesforcedx-vscode-apex-testing (+512 ms / +400%): Consistently higher in the "with" scenario (349/810/759 ms vs. 79/163/141 ms). However, the absolute values are small and the Without R1 value of 79 ms was from a lazy activation. R2/R3 comparison: Without 152 ms vs. With 785 ms. This warrants monitoring but is not attributable to UI Preview since it does not interact with the Apex testing extension.
  • salesforce-metadata-visualizer-vscode (+327 ms / +272%): The metadata visualizer activated and processed XML files in dreamhouse; its activation time depends on which XML files VS Code happened to open. Not related to UI Preview.

Conclusion

Comparing R2/R3 only (excluding the Without R1 cold-start outlier) provides the most reliable view:

MetricAggregate R2/R3 DeltaAssessment
Load Code-138 ms (-1.6%)Flat -- no regression
Call ActivateNo change (0-53 ms range)Flat -- VM overhead on apex-testing in both scenarios
Finish Activate-279 ms (-0.6%)Flat -- no regression

The salesforcedx-vscode-ui-preview extension (v1.1.4) has no measurable negative impact on Salesforce extension startup performance on Windows. Its own activation cost on Windows is approximately 354 ms Load Code + 334 ms Finish Activate.

The elevated salesforcedx-vscode-apex-testing Finish Activate in the "with" scenario (+633 ms in R2/R3) is the only notable anomaly but is not consistently directional with UI Preview across the macOS test (where apex-testing showed no change), suggesting it is a Windows VM scheduling artifact rather than an interaction with UI Preview.
